key: Ye will not attain unto piety until ye spend of that which ye love.
s: After a ransom of gold is refused to those dying in disbelief, the surah turns to giving; al-Tabari, on 3:92, reads the piety as Allah’s kindness in bringing them into His Garden, reached by giving from the wealth they most wish to keep.
src: al-Tabari, Jāmiʿ al-bayān, on 3:92, the Arabic text of the Tarteel QUL library via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

evidence.words: يعني بذلك جل ثناؤه: لن تدركوا، أيها المؤمنون، البرَّ = وهو"البر" من الله الذي يطلبونه منه بطاعتهم إياه وعبادتهم له ويرجونه منه، وذلك تفضّله عليهم بإدخالهم جنته، وصرف عذابه عنهم.
evidence.gloss: By it He, exalted be His praise, means: you will not attain, O believers, al-birr, which is the kindness from God that they seek from Him by their obedience and worship of Him and hope for from Him, and that is His favour to them in bringing them into His Garden and turning His punishment away from them.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al 'Imran 3:92, at 384). Plain sense faithful: 3:91 says the earth full of gold would not be accepted as ransom from those who die in disbelief, and 3:92 turns to spending; no four-word run from the verse. In the packet on 3:92 al-Tabari glosses al-birr as God’s kindness, His favour in bringing them into His Garden and turning His punishment from them (the words above), cites those who say al-birr is the Garden, and then gives his own paraphrase: you will not reach your Lord’s Garden until you give in alms from what you love and wish to have for yourselves, of your choicest wealth. The sentence carries both halves; ‘most wish to keep’ is a fair paraphrase of that without drift. The proposer’s basis joined two passages with an ellipsis; the evidence here is one contiguous span. 43 words; entry-check ok.
